title: Resolvers
description: Write resolvers to fetch and return data.

data.text: A resolver is the function that produces the value for a field. In Hot Chocolate, resolvers can be methods, properties, or even separate resolver classes.
The simplest resolver is a method on your type class. The method name matches the field name by default.

data.title: Field Resolver
data.content: Resolve the author name inside Book.

data.text: Hot Chocolate provides special parameter bindings: `[Service]` to inject services, `[Parent]` to access the parent object, and `[ScopedService]` for scoped services.
Hot Chocolate supports pipeline-style resolvers using `Use...` attributes. This lets you compose operations like projection, paging, and filtering.

data.title: Pipeline Resolver
When to Use a Separate Resolver
data.text: Use a separate resolver class when the logic is complex or reused across multiple types. Simpler fields can stay as methods on the type class.

terms.definition: A function that provides the value for a GraphQL field.
